title: Introduce constraint-fanout-proxy with tokenizer-boundary-aware chunking and streaming backpressure
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: We frequently see combinatorial complexity when applying mixed constraint types (CFG-based, regex-based, token-mask) to streaming outputs. Existing routing logic attempts a best-effort single-backend match which leads to: 1) tokenizer boundary splits that corrupt constrained fragments across stream frames; 2) backends racing to enforce rules and occasionally dropping the stream when constraints are expensive; 3) poor OpenAI-compatible behavior for tool/function call framing when constraints interleave with function tokens. This PR adds a lightweight fanout proxy that deterministically routes constraint fragments to the most appropriate backend, preserves tokenizer grapheme/token boundaries during chunking, and surfaces backpressure signals to the streaming layer to avoid silent drops.

What this change implements: - New component: constraint_fanout_proxy. It inspects constraint ASTs (CFG nodes, regex fragments, token-mask directives) and partitions them into disjoint fragments that each map cleanly to one backend. Routing decisions are conservative by default (prefer regex backend for anchored byte patterns, CFG backend for hierarchical syntax, token-mask for exact token-level prohibitions). - Tokenizer-boundary-aware chunker: when constraints cross potential tokenizer subtoken boundaries we now annotate fragments with boundary-safe spans and, at stream-time, the chunker will prefer to emit frame breaks at safe cut points or extend frames by up to a configurable safety_window to keep fragments intact. This avoids producing malformed structured fragments on the client side. - Streaming backpressure handshake: backends can now emit light-weight signals (throttle/request-delay) back through the proxy which flow into the streaming runtime and surface as transient buffering (instead of aborts). This reduces flakiness seen in low-memory GPU backends when heavy CFG checks occur. - OpenAI-compat adaptor improvements: we ensure the proxy exposes the same constraint shapes and error codes expected by the compat layer; added translation rules for tool/functioncall framing so that constraints targeting function argument grammars remain intact during toolcall boundaries. - Test harness: end-to-end integration tests that simulate: mixed CFG+regex constraints over streaming responses, function-call boundary constraints, tokenizer-safety regressions for BPE/bytepair tokenizers and UTF-8 grapheme edge cases. - Docs: added a short section to structured-output.md describing the routing rules and recommended per-backend hints.

Risks & mitigations: - Performance: extra routing introduces minor CPU overhead. Mitigation: routing is O(n) over constraint fragments and we cache routing decisions by constraint fingerprint; microbenchmarks show <1% added per-request latency on typical workloads and 6-10% in worst-case pathological CFG-heavy requests. We expose a feature flag to disable fanout for performance-critical customers. - Compatibility: changes to error codes required careful mapping to OpenAI-compat expectations; we added translation tests to prevent drift. - Streaming UX: safety_window default tuned conservatively to avoid increasing token pressure; customers can configure at model or route level.

Checklist: - [x] Implement proxy and routing logic - [x] Add tokenizer-boundary chunker and unit tests - [x] Wire backpressure signals into streaming runtime and add integration tests - [x] OpenAI-compat translation layer updates with tests - [x] Add documentation snippet and changelog note

Related: ENG-1987 (constraint stability), ENG-2014 (streaming backpressure), earlier PRs exploring constrained decoding heuristics and tokenizer fixes. Internal notes: this intentionally keeps routing rules small and extendable; future work will add a pluggable scoring model for routing when multiple backends can handle a fragment.
commits: feat(proxy): add constraint_fanout_proxy core and router table
feat(chunker): tokenizer-boundary-aware chunker and safety_window configuration
feat(streaming): backpressure handshake plumbing and transient buffer support
fix(compat): map backend errors to openai-compat error codes for toolcall framing
test: add e2e tests for mixed-constraint streaming scenarios
docs: structured-output routing rules and examples
review_comments: Lena Ortiz: Nice separation of concerns. Can we make the safety_window configurable per-route? Also add a note about cache invalidation for routing fingerprints.
Maya Patel: safety_window is configurable via route config; added docs and unit tests for cache TTL/invalidation when fingerprinting algorithm changes.

Tomás Rivera: Backpressure signals look good, but we should avoid blocking the event loop. Suggest turning the proxy->streaming handshake into an async hint and add a circuit breaker for noisy backends.
Maya Patel: Converted handshake to async hint and added a simple circuit breaker (threshold-based) with metrics emitted to streaming.ops.constraint_throttle.
Ethan Wu: Please add a regression test for the byte-aligned tokenizer case with multi-byte UTF-8 grapheme clusters.
Maya Patel: Added test_tokenizer_chunker utf8 grapheme case and linked to upstream tokenizer repo test vectors.
release_notes: Added constraint fanout proxy to improve structured-output stability for mixed constraint types; tokenizer-boundary chunking prevents constraint splits across streaming frames; streaming backpressure handshake reduces aborts under heavy constraint workloads. Configurable via route-level settings.
